readback.name: Poincare.ParabolicSpatialHolderPullback.exists_spatial_Y_pullback
readback.mathematical_statement: Let E3 be EuclideanSpace R (Fin 3), the real three-dimensional Euclidean vector space. For arbitrary universe v, let V : Type v be any normed additive commutative group equipped with a normed real vector-space structure. No CompleteSpace V assumption is present. Let F : E3 -> E3 be any total globally C-infinity function with compact topological support, meaning the closure of the locus F(x) != 0 is compact. F is not required to be linear, affine, injective, invertible, or a coordinate transition. C-infinity is ContDiff at the ENat top injected into WithTop ENat. For every real alpha with 0 <= alpha, there exists a real C >= 0 such that for every real T there exists a continuous real-linear map Q : Y alpha T V -> Y alpha T V whose operator norm is at most C and which satisfies (Q f)(t,x) = f(t,F(x)) for every f in Y alpha T V and every (t,x) in R x E3. In particular, the asserted operator is linear in f even when F is nonlinear. The bound C is chosen before T and is uniform in T, f, and the evaluation point. The quantifier order permits C to depend on V and its instances, on F, and on alpha; no uniformity in these inputs or explicit formula for C is asserted. All real T are covered, without a positivity assumption. The cylinder is Icc 0 T times all of E3; for T < 0 it is empty and for T = 0 it is the entire spatial slice at time zero. Y is the pinned graph space of total V-valued functions on R x E3 that vanish off this cylinder and have bounded values and bounded scaled differences inside it. Its norm is the sum of the value supremum on the cylinder and the alpha-Hoelder seminorm on distinct ordered cylinder pairs, with the seminorm denominator D(p,q)^alpha for D((t,x),(s,y)) = norm(x-y) + sqrt(abs(t-s)). Inserting zero in the supremum definitions handles the empty set. Y has no separate smoothness, approximation, or continuity condition; the Hoelder condition applies only to pairs inside the cylinder and does not impose continuity of the zero extension across the time endpoints. Alpha = 0 is included, and no upper bound alpha < 1 or alpha <= 1 is imposed. The evaluation identity is on the entire ambient product, not merely on the cylinder. It preserves time and is consistent with the required zero extension because (t,x) and (t,F(x)) have the same time coordinate. There is no scalar cutoff factor or source weight in this identity. Compact support of F does not assert compact spatial support of Q f: wherever F(x) = 0, the identity gives (Q f)(t,x) = f(t,0), which need not vanish. No derivative transport, jet norm estimate, atlas compatibility, inverse operator, or small operator norm is claimed.
